computed_from.$comment: main at the time this manifest was prepared; every digest and blob sha below was read from this tree, not from a working directory.

design_cutoff.$comment: §1.1. What was knowable to the preregistration's author. An epistemic fact. NEVER changes — changing it would claim E5 was designed with information it did not have. DISTINCT from freeze_base_sha below; equating them is the defect recorded as topology log entry 1.

freeze_anchor.$comment: §14.2. Which state of the default branch the freeze is anchored to, topologically. A git fact, changed only by the recorded successor procedure.

topology_amendment_log.reason: initial value, equated with E5_DESIGN_CUTOFF_SHA. Superseded: the E1-v5 PR merged first, landing f670258f on main as an ordinary merge with first parent 8f5aaed. Clause (b) became unsatisfiable for any future merge.
the tip of main after that merge.

M_evidence.$comment: §14.2 (a)-(f), recomputed by scanning every commit reachable from computed_from.tree. 89 commits scanned; exactly one candidate.

spec_revisions.$comment: §5.1, §1.2. Git object names (SHA-1, 40 hex) — blob shas, not SHA-256 digests.

spec_revision.role: the spec_revision every SPEC_REQUIRED_BINDING fact carries (§5.1, §5.4)

artifact_digest_method.$comment: Deliberately NOT JCS. §5.5's JCS+SHA-256 governs fact_id and fact_bundle_digest, values whose purpose is stability under re-serialization. An ARTIFACT digest wants the opposite property: reformatting an artifact must invalidate its digest rather than silently preserving identity. Recorded explicitly so no later reader 'canonicalizes' these files and arrives at a different identity for the same object.

capability_boundary.$comment: §9.3, by reference and digest. Declarations only — no bodies exist. M0 therefore pins the CONTRACT, not the code, so writing the bodies later does not invalidate this manifest.

fact_resolver_declaration.declares: interface FactResolver { Resolve(id: FactId): Fact | NotFound }
fact_resolver_declaration.K3: exactly one operation; no iterator, length, count, key set, collection-valued member, or operation returning more than one Fact

bundle_loader_exported_signature.signature: export declare function load(bytes: Uint8Array): { resolver: FactResolver; digest: string }

canonicalization_and_digest.$comment: §5.5. Distinct from artifact_digest_method above; see that entry.

s2_deny_list.$comment: §11.2 S2. Five frozen categories, and no sixth. Each entry records the frozen category text verbatim plus its TypeScript/Node realisation. The categories are denied in the VERIFIER's transitive closure (shell and kernel); they do not constrain the producer or the extractor, which are outside the independence surface.
s2_deny_list.authoring_rule: This manifest records the frozen categories and their language realisation. It does NOT redefine, narrow or widen any category. Deciding mechanically whether a given occurrence falls inside a category belongs to the S2 check implementation, not to manifest authoring.

categories.category: dynamic code evaluation, or code loading not resolvable statically

typescript_realization: the node:fs/promises equivalents of the above
applicability: The frozen category names WRITE. Reads are outside it — §11.1's clean-room run hands the verifier files to read. This restates the frozen scope and does not narrow it.

categories.category: reflection, dynamic member access, or serialization round-trip used to reach past a declared interface
applicability: The frozen semantic predicate above applies unchanged: the category is these constructs USED TO REACH PAST A DECLARED INTERFACE.
Ordinary traversal of raw parsed data is not prohibited merely because the same language construct is used. The loader must parse a plain JSON object at V5; that is not reaching past an interface.

NO narrowing by the expression's current static type is introduced here. Aliasing, casts or type laundering do not move an operation outside category (v) when it is used to reach past a declared interface — `const x: any = resolver; Reflect.get(x, ...)` is inside the category, and a static-type predicate would wrongly exempt it.
The flow/type analysis that mechanically decides 'used to reach past' belongs to the S2 check implementation, not to this manifest.

frozen_surfaces_by_reference.$comment: §14.3 requires these by reference to the preregistration's sections and its blob sha, not by transcription. The authority is the document at E5_DOC_BLOB_SHA.

spec_facts_identity.$comment: NOT an M0-pinned protocol surface. §14.3 enumerates the byte-pinned artifacts — the ruleset, the two schemas, and the two capability declarations — and this is not among them. Adding it would create a new protocol surface after the freeze.

normative_identity.note: §5.4 already defines all 27 facts, including their spec_revision. That is the authority.

transcription_artifact.status: transcription artifact — NOT an additional M0-pinned protocol surface
transcription_artifact.note: verify-m0.py may emit this file's git blob and SHA-256 as INFORMATIONAL audit output. Neither is an M0 obligation and neither gates anything.

spec_facts_identity.why_this_is_not_a_gap: At a real run the facts enter a bundle whose digest is pinned in E5-M1, and the extractor and producer revisions are pinned per run (§14.3). A later change to the transcription artifact is therefore a change of implementation or of an input bundle — recorded as such — not a silent substitution of frozen §5.4.
